mainTopic: What comes out of a non-kosher animal: donkey urine, bee honey, deer lumps, a donkey's birth sac, and a fish found inside another fish.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב ששת's ruling that donkey urine is forbidden. In a second version (איכא דאמרי), he bases the ruling on the rule 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא': what comes from a non-kosher animal is non-kosher. The גמרא challenges him from bee honey, which a ברייתא permits because bees only carry the nectar and do not produce it. The answer is that רב ששת follows רבי יעקב, who learns from the פסוק 'אך את זה תאכלו' that honey is a special Torah exception. That exception covers only plain 'honey', meaning bee honey, and not the honey of גזין and wasps. Next come other things that leave an animal's body: lumps from a fallow deer, which רב ספרא explains are a hart's semen, and a donkey's birth sac, which רב הונא permits as a mere secretion. A ברייתא about the skin over a human newborn's face supports רב הונא. Finally, a new משנה rules on a fish found inside another fish. The גמרא discusses when we worry that a non-kosher fish gave birth to the fish found inside it, and gives four answers, ending with רב אשי's רוב that fish give birth to their own species.

steps.title: Donkey urine is included as a type of non-kosher substance
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of רב ששת's first-version answer. The words 'מן הטמא' teach that any type (מין) of substance from a טמא animal is forbidden, and donkey urine is one of those types.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...the non-kosher.' And these fluids too are a type of the non-kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the middle of a sentence. רב ששת is finishing his answer: donkey urine counts as a 'type' of non-kosher substance, so it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת reads the word 'מן' in 'מן הטמא' as 'מִין', meaning 'any type of'. That widens the איסור beyond the animal's meat to things that come out of it. Donkey urine resembles donkey milk, which is already forbidden, so it falls under the same category.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The word 'הטמא' is the last word of a פסוק quoted on the previous amud, not a new statement.

phrases.english: '...the non-kosher.'
phrases.notes: End of the quoted פסוק, read as 'מן הטמא' (from the non-kosher).

phrases.english: And these (fluids) too are a type of the non-kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's answer earlier (first version).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Donkey urine is a 'type' of non-kosher substance included in 'מן הטמא', so it is forbidden.

steps.title: Second version: the question was only about donkey urine
steps.stepSummary: A second version (איכא דאמרי) says the students had no doubt about horse or camel urine, since nobody drinks it. Their real question was about donkey urine, which people drink as medicine for ירקונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: about horses and camels they had no question, because people don't drink it. Their question was about a donkey's urine, which people drink and which helps against jaundice. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a different version of the question that was put to רב ששת. In this version the question is narrower and focuses only on the donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Horses and camels are left out because, as the text says, nobody drinks their urine, so the question has no practical relevance. Donkey urine is a real case: people drink it for healing. Because it is useful, someone might think the חכמים would not have forbidden it, so the question is a real one.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (introduces a second version)
They were in doubt / they asked

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question added on top of the first one. It is a different report of the same discussion with רב ששת.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּסוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ,
phrases.english: about (urine of) horses and camels they had no question,
since people do not drink it.
When they asked, it was about (urine) of a donkey,
which people drink and which is good for jaundice,
what (is the law)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the question answered in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is donkey urine, which is drunk for its healing value, forbidden?

steps.title: רב ששת: what comes from a non-kosher animal is non-kosher
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers from the rule 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא': whatever comes out of a non-kosher animal is forbidden. Donkey urine comes from a non-kosher animal, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You already learned it: what comes from the non-kosher is non-kosher, and what comes from the kosher is kosher. And these too come from a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the second-version question. He tells the students that a rule they already learned settles it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רב ששת does not use the פסוק. He relies on the well-known rule that whatever comes out of a טמא animal takes on its status. Because donkey urine comes from a donkey, it is forbidden. Its medical usefulness does not change that.

keyTerms.meaning: What comes from a non-kosher animal is non-kosher

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא' is the central principle of this whole topic. The next challenge will test exactly how far it reaches.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it:
That which comes from the non-kosher is non-kosher,
and that which comes from the kosher is kosher,
and these too come from a non-kosher (animal).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Donkey urine is forbidden because it comes from a non-kosher animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: היוצא מן הטמא טמא applies to donkey urine.

steps.title: Challenge from bee honey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת from a ברייתא. Bee honey is permitted because bees only carry the nectar inside their bodies and do not produce it. By the same logic, urine that merely passes through the donkey should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Why did they say bee honey is permitted? Because the bees bring it into their bodies, but they do not produce it from their bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an objection (מיתיבי) against רב ששת's ruling. It uses a ברייתא that explains why bee honey is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bees are non-kosher, yet their honey is permitted, because the honey is only stored nectar and not a product of the bee's body. The challenge reasons that donkey urine may also be just water that passed through the body unchanged. If so, it should be permitted, which goes against רב ששת's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (an objection from a ברייתא)
They bring it into their bodies
They produce it from their bodies

steps.confusionAlert: According to this ברייתא, bee honey is not a special exception to 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא'. It falls outside the rule entirely, because the bee does not produce it and only carries it. The challenge is that donkey urine may fall outside the rule in the same way. The source text only states the bee-honey rule; the application to the donkey is understood from context.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
For what reason did they say
that bee honey is permitted?
Because they bring it into their bodies,
but do not produce it from their bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that donkey urine is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something that only passes through a non-kosher body and is not produced by it is permitted, as bee honey shows. Donkey urine may be just like that, so it should be permitted.

steps.title: רב ששת follows רבי יעקב: honey is a special Torah exception
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds like רבי יעקב, who says honey is permitted only because the Torah specifically allowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said his ruling following רבי יעקב, who says: honey, the Torah specifically permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from bee honey. רב ששת does not accept the reason 'bees only carry it'. He holds that honey is permitted only because the Torah made a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed honey is allowed for a logical reason: it just passes through the bee. If that were true, the same reason would apply to donkey urine. But if honey is allowed only by a special verse (a one-time exception), the general rule 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא' still stands everywhere else, so donkey urine stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah / ה׳
He said his ruling following the view of...

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reasons for honey. The ברייתא in step 4 said honey is allowed because bees only carry it. רבי יעקב says it is allowed only because of a special פסוק. רב ששת follows רבי יעקב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רב ששת can keep 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא' as a full rule: honey is an exception, not a hole in the rule.

phrases.english: He (Rav Sheshet) spoke following Rabbi Yaakov,
who says: honey, the Torah specifically permitted it.
phrases.notes: A special exception, not a logical rule

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from bee honey in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the ruling to a תנא with a different reason for the source case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Honey is permitted because bees only carry it, so donkey urine should be permitted too
steps.terutzMaskana: Honey is permitted only by a special Torah exception, so donkey urine remains forbidden

steps.title: רבי יעקב's ברייתא: the verse about winged creatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יעקב's ברייתא, which reads 'זה' in the פסוק as excluding non-kosher winged creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יעקב says, 'Only this may you eat of all winged swarming creatures.' This you may eat, but you may not eat a non-kosher winged swarming creature.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי יעקב's view. This step sets up the first reading of the פסוק, which the גמרא will question next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זה' ('this') limits what is allowed. At first glance it seems to teach only that non-kosher winged creatures are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yaakov says:
'Only this may you eat'
'of all winged swarming creatures' (ויקרא 11:21)
this you may eat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא.
phrases.english: but you may not eat a non-kosher winged swarming creature.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא behind רבי יעקב's view
steps.raayaObject: רבי יעקב's view that honey is a special Torah exception

steps.title: That prohibition is already written clearly
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition of non-kosher winged creatures is already stated openly, so why read it from 'זה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-kosher winged swarming creature is already written explicitly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the simple reading. The Torah already forbids non-kosher winged creatures in a separate פסוק, so 'זה' should not be needed for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words. If a law is already stated openly (ויקרא 11:20), the extra word must be teaching something new. This pushes us toward a new reading.

phrases.english: A non-kosher winged creature is already written explicitly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading in step 6 as unnecessary
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'זה' as forbidding non-kosher winged creatures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That law is already explicit elsewhere, so the derivation would be redundant

steps.title: What a non-kosher flying creature produces is allowed: bee honey
steps.stepSummary: The new reading: you may not eat the creature, but you may eat what it produces, which is bee honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a non-kosher winged creature you may not eat, but you may eat what a non-kosher winged creature discharges. And what is that? That is bee honey.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the פסוק in a new way. The creature itself is forbidden, but something that comes out of it is allowed, and that thing is bee honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the special Torah exception רב ששת relies on. Honey is permitted because a פסוק says so, not because of any general logic. That is why the exception does not spread to donkey urine.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא אִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: Rather, a non-kosher winged creature you may not eat,
but you may eat
what a non-kosher winged creature discharges,
and what is that? That is bee honey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא אִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the redundancy by giving the word a new meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זה' only repeats the ban on non-kosher winged creatures
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זה' permits what the creature produces: bee honey

steps.title: Is the honey of other insects also allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the honey of גזין and wasps is also permitted, and answers no.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that even the honey of גזין and wasps is permitted. You said: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא checks how far the exception goes. Could other honey-making insects be included too? It answers no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since honey is a special exception, its limits must be set carefully. The ברייתא rules out other insects' honey first, and gives its reason in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (a possible mistaken idea)
A type of honey-making insect (a kind of bee or hornet)

phrases.english: One might think even the honey of gizzin and wasps is permitted?
You said: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limits of the honey exception
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the exception include other insects' honey?

steps.title: Why include bees but leave out the others?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason there is to include bee honey and exclude the honey of גזין and wasps.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to include bees, and to exclude גזין and wasps?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for the reason behind its line. All these insects are non-kosher and make honey, so why treat them differently? This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זה' includes only one thing. The question is which honey it points to and how we know.

phrases.english: And what did you see to include bees,
and to exclude gizzin and wasps?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 9's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for including bees and excluding other insects

steps.title: Plain 'honey' means bee honey
steps.stepSummary: Bee honey is called just 'honey', while other insects' honey always needs an added name, so only bee honey is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include bee honey, which has no added name. And I exclude the honey of גזין and wasps, which have an added name.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: when people say just 'honey', they mean bee honey. Other honey always needs a label like 'wasp honey', so it is not the main 'honey' the Torah allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exception is limited to what is plainly called 'honey'. A name that needs a modifier shows a secondary kind. That kind is not included in the special permission.

keyTerms.meaning: An added name, a modifier (like 'wasp' in 'wasp honey')

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת follows רבי יעקב: bee honey is permitted only because of a special פסוק (אך את זה תאכלו). The exception covers only plain 'honey', meaning bee honey. So 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא' still forbids donkey urine.

phrases.english: I include bee honey
which has no added modifier name,
and I exclude the honey of gizzin and wasps
which has an added modifier name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Plain 'honey' refers to bee honey. Other honeys need a modifier and are excluded.

steps.title: Whose view permits the honey of גזין and wasps?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that calls the honey of גזין and wasps טהור and permitted to eat, and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what a ברייתא teaches: 'The honey of גזין and wasps is טהור and permitted to eat'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a different ברייתא that permits the honey of גזין and wasps. It asks whose opinion this ברייתא follows, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 9-11, the ברייתא we just learned said that only bee honey is permitted and that the honey of גזין and wasps is forbidden. This new ברייתא says the opposite, so the גמרא needs to know which תנא it follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of stinging insect similar to a hornet
Here: cannot become impure (טמא) as food

phrases.english: Whose opinion does this follow, which is taught:
The honey of gizzin and wasps
is ritually pure and permitted to be eaten?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that disagrees with the conclusion of steps 9-11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא permits the honey of גזין and wasps

steps.title: It does not follow רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that permits this honey goes against רבי יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not like רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא does not follow רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב's view, which the גמרא learned just before this, includes only bee honey and leaves out the honey of גזין and wasps. A ברייתא that permits their honey must therefore come from a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view excluded non-bee honey

phrases.english: Not in accordance with Rabbi Ya'akov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows a תנא other than רבי יעקב

steps.title: The word טהור shows that this honey needs intention
steps.stepSummary: Because the ברייתא calls this honey טהור, it must need someone's intention to eat it before it can become impure as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'טהור.' So it seems that this honey needs intention to become food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's word 'טהור' and learns a rule from it about טומאת אוכלין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something only gets food-טומאה if it counts as food. Honey of גזין and wasps is not normally eaten, so it counts as food only when a person decides to eat it (מחשבה). Without that decision it stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs intention, meaning a decision to use it as food

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'טהור' does not mean 'kosher.' It means the honey cannot become ritually impure, because without intention it is not counted as food.

phrases.english: 'It is pure' —
evidently it requires intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Learns a further point from the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honey of גזין and wasps becomes food for טומאה only through intention

steps.title: Support: bee honey in the hive needs no intention
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that bee honey, even while still in the hive, receives food-טומאה without any intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: Honey in its hive becomes impure with food-impurity even without intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the idea that intention matters. Bee honey needs no intention, so other honey does need it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People normally eat bee honey, so it counts as food automatically, even before it is taken out of the hive. The contrast fits step 14: honey that is not normally eaten, like that of גזין and wasps, needs a person's intention to count as food.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity that applies to food

steps.whatToRemember: Bee honey counts as food automatically. Honey of גזין and wasps counts as food only through intention.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
Honey in its hive
becomes impure with food-impurity
without intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the inference of step 14
steps.raayaObject: Whether intention matters for honey to count as food
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: bee honey in its hive receives food-טומאה without intention

steps.title: The רבנן assumed the deer's discharge was forbidden eggs
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן first thought that lumps discharged from a female fallow deer were its eggs, and so forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the lumps from a female fallow deer, the רבנן thought to say: they are eggs, and they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case of something that comes out of an animal. It reports the רבנן's first assumption, which sets up רב ספרא's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lumps were eggs from the deer's own body, they would be part of a living animal, and so forbidden. This is only an initial assumption ('סבור'), which signals that it will be corrected.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן thought to say (an initial assumption)

phrases.english: Lumps from a female fallow deer,
the Sages thought to say:
they are eggs, and are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: another thing that comes out of an animal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial view: the deer's lumps are eggs and are forbidden

steps.title: רב ספרא: it is a hart's semen, not the deer's eggs
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא explains that the lumps are hardened semen from a hart that mated with the fallow deer, so they are not part of the deer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: It is the seed of a hart. The hart chases the hind, but since her womb is narrow she cannot mate with it. So it chases the fallow deer, and the seed falls out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא rejects the רבנן's assumption and explains where the lumps really come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lumps are not the deer's own body tissue. They are semen from a different animal that hardened and fell out. Because they were never part of the deer, the reason for forbidding them falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who explains the case

steps.whyThisMatters: The worry was that the lumps were the deer's own eggs, making them part of a living animal (אבר מן החי). Once רב ספרא shows they are a hart's semen and were never part of the deer's body, that concern falls away.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
It is the seed of a hart,
which goes after the hind,
and since her womb is narrow
she does not mate,
and it goes after the fallow deer
and they fall out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא זַרְעָא דְּאַיָּלָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption of step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The identification of the lumps as eggs, and the prohibition that follows from it
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lumps are a hart's hardened semen, not the deer's own eggs

steps.title: רב הונא permits the donkey's birth sac
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the skin that comes out over a newborn donkey's face is permitted, because it is only a secretion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The skin that comes out over the face of a donkey is permitted. What is the reason? It is just a secretion.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new ruling about another thing that comes out of an animal, and the גמרא gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally anything from a non-kosher animal like a donkey is forbidden. But this birth sac is not a real part of the mother or the baby. It is only a discharge, so it does not carry the donkey's prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this ruling
The skin that comes out over its face (the birth sac)

steps.whatToRemember: A secretion, meaning something that comes out of an animal but is not part of its body, does not take on the status of a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹר הַבָּא כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל חֲמוֹר —
phrases.english: The skin that comes opposite the face of a donkey —
is permitted,
what is the reason?
It is merely a secretion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא עוֹר הַבָּא כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל חֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case in the same theme of animal secretions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The birth sac of a donkey is permitted because it is only a secretion

steps.title: רב חסדא brings a ברייתא about the skin over a human newborn's face
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא supports רב הונא with a ברייתא saying the skin over a human newborn's face is טהור, whether the baby is alive or dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: A ברייתא supports you. 'The skin that comes over the face of a person, whether alive or dead, is pure.' Doesn't this mean: whether the baby is alive and its mother is alive, or the baby is dead and its mother is dead?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a ברייתא to back up רב הונא's ruling that this skin is only a secretion. He reads the words 'alive or dead' as meaning both baby and mother together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the skin is טהור even when the baby and the mother are both dead, it cannot be part of either body, since then it would carry טומאת מת. So it must be a mere secretion, exactly as רב הונא said.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that supports you
The skin that comes out over the newborn's face
Is it not that... (introduces the reading used for a proof)
Ritually pure; here, it does not carry corpse-impurity

steps.whyThisMatters: The proof depends completely on how 'alive or dead' is read. This sets up the exchange that follows.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him (to Rav Huna):
A baraita is taught that supports you:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹר הַבָּא כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: The skin that comes over the face of a person (a newborn),
whether alive or dead, is pure.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ חַיָּה,
phrases.english: Does it not mean: whether the baby is alive and its mother is alive,
or the baby is dead and its mother is dead?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב הונא's ruling in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that the skin over a newborn donkey's face is a mere secretion and therefore permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that calls the skin over a human newborn's face טהור whether alive or dead

steps.title: רב הונא reads the ברייתא differently
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that 'alive or dead' may mean only one of the two is alive, so the ברייתא proves nothing about when both are dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means: whether the baby is alive and its mother is dead, or the baby is dead and its mother is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes away the proof brought for his own view. He offers another way to read 'alive or dead.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, one of the two is always alive. The skin could still be part of the living one's body and so be טהור. That means the ברייתא does not show the skin is a mere secretion, since if both were dead it might be טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: No, the proof does not work (opens a rejection)

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is rejecting a proof for HIS OWN ruling. He is not changing his view; he is only saying this ברייתא is not clear enough to prove it.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ מֵתָה,
phrases.english: No: whether the baby is alive and its mother is dead,
or the baby is dead and its mother is alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא used in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof, not the ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Alive or dead' could mean only one of them is alive, so the case of both dead is not covered

steps.title: רב חסדא quotes an explicit ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes another ברייתא that clearly says 'baby alive and mother alive, or baby dead and mother dead.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: whether the baby is alive and its mother is alive, or the baby is dead and its mother is dead!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers רב הונא's other reading by quoting a ברייתא that spells out the exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא openly includes the case where both are dead, so the other reading from step 20 no longer works. The skin is טהור even then, so it must be a mere secretion.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא...!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ חַיָּה,
phrases.english: But it was taught: whether the baby is alive and its mother is alive,
or the baby is dead and its mother is dead!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 20 and brings back the proof from step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that the skin is a mere secretion
steps.raayaSupportSource: An explicit ברייתא that includes the case where both baby and mother are dead

steps.title: רב הונא accepts the explicit ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says: if that is what the ברייתא says, then it says so, and the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was taught, it was taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא agrees that the clear ברייתא settles the matter. This closes the discussion about the skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue with an explicit ברייתא. The result is that his ruling now has clear support: the skin is טהור even when both are dead, because it is only a secretion.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was taught, it was taught; I accept it

steps.whatToRemember: The skin over a newborn's face is not part of the baby's or mother's body. It is a mere secretion, so it is טהור, and for an animal it is permitted. A clear ברייתא supports this.

phrases.english: If it was taught, it was taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the explicit ברייתא from step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The explicit ברייתא confirms רב הונא's ruling that the skin is a mere secretion.

steps.title: A fish found inside another fish
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a kosher fish swallowed by a non-kosher fish is permitted. A non-kosher fish swallowed by a kosher fish is forbidden, because the outer fish is not where it grew.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish: the kosher fish may be eaten. A kosher fish that swallowed a non-kosher fish: the non-kosher fish may not be eaten, because it did not grow from the kosher fish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It rules on a fish found inside another fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is where the fish came from, not where it was found. Something swallowed is not a product of the fish that swallowed it, so each fish keeps its own status.
steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the theme of the פרק: something that comes from a non-kosher creature is forbidden, but only if it really grew from it.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ דָּג טָמֵא שֶׁבָּלַע דָּג טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: A non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish:
the kosher fish is permitted to be eaten,
and a kosher fish that swallowed a non-kosher fish:
the non-kosher fish is forbidden to be eaten,
because it did not grow from the outer fish.
phrases.notes: The swallowed fish is not a product of the fish that swallowed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ דָּג טָמֵא שֶׁבָּלַע דָּג טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A swallowed fish keeps its own kosher status, because it did not grow from the fish that swallowed it.

steps.title: Only if we saw the swallowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the kosher fish is permitted only because we saw it being swallowed. If not, we assume the non-kosher fish gave birth to it, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The reason is that we saw it swallow. But if we did not see it swallow, we say it spawned it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the wording of the משנה. It limits the permission to a case where we saw the swallowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's word 'swallowed' means we know it was swallowed. If we never saw that, the simplest explanation is that the non-kosher fish gave birth to the small fish inside it. Its offspring are also non-kosher and forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא's discussion of the משנה
The reason is that we saw it
But if not... (introduces the opposite case)
It spawned it; it gave birth to it

steps.whatToRemember: According to this inference, a kosher fish found inside a non-kosher fish is permitted only if we saw it being swallowed. רב אשי (step 30) disagrees and permits it even without seeing.
steps.confusionAlert: Even a fish that looks kosher is forbidden if we assume it was born from a non-kosher fish. What decides is where it came from, not how it looks.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The reason is that we saw that it swallowed it,
but if we did not see that it swallowed it,
we say: it spawned it.
phrases.notes: So the small fish is treated as offspring of the non-kosher fish and is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Infers a limit on the משנה in step 23 from its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without seeing the swallowing, a fish found inside a non-kosher fish is assumed to be its offspring and is forbidden.

steps.title: Source that non-kosher fish give birth to live young
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the worry that the non-kosher fish gave birth to the fish found inside it. It answers with a ברייתא: a דג טמא gives birth to live young, while a דג טהור lays eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? As a ברייתא teaches: a non-kosher fish gives birth to live young, and a kosher fish lays eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants a source for what it said in step 24. Without seeing the swallowing, we would worry that the non-kosher fish gave birth to the fish inside it. The ברייתא shows that non-kosher fish give birth to live young inside their bodies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kosher fish lay eggs outside their bodies, so a fish found inside another fish was never born there from a kosher fish. Non-kosher fish carry their babies inside and give birth to them live. That is why finding a fish inside a non-kosher fish raises a real worry that it is that fish's own baby.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know this? As it is taught:
phrases.notes: The question asks for the source of the worry raised in step 24.

phrases.english: A non-kosher fish gives birth to live young,
a kosher fish lays eggs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the worry inferred in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: The worry that a fish found inside a non-kosher fish may be its own offspring.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a דג טמא gives birth to live young, while a דג טהור lays eggs.

steps.title: Even after seeing the swallowing, maybe the found fish was born there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference. If non-kosher fish give birth to live young, then even when we saw the swallowing, we should worry. Maybe the swallowed fish was digested, and the fish we found was born inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even when we saw it swallow, we should say: that swallowed fish was digested, and this one we found, the non-kosher fish gave birth to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the worry one step further. It challenges the ruling of the משנה that the fish is permitted when we saw the swallowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing the swallowing only proves that some kosher fish went in. It does not prove that the fish we found is the same fish. The swallowed one may have been digested, and this one may be the non-kosher fish's baby.

phrases.english: If so,
even when we saw that it swallowed, we should say:
that one (the swallowed fish) was digested,
and this one (the fish we found), it gave birth to it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כִּי חָזֵינָא דִּבְלַע אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 25 to attack the ruling of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the משנה that the fish is permitted when we saw it being swallowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seeing a fish swallowed does not prove that the fish we found is that same fish. It could still be the non-kosher fish's own baby.

steps.title: רב ששת: the fish was found in the digestive tract
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the משנה speaks of a fish found in the digestive tract. That is not where a non-kosher fish carries its babies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: the case is where he found it in the digestive tract.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge by narrowing the case of the משנה. The fish was found in a place where babies never grow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Babies grow in the womb area, not in the digestive tract. A fish found in the digestive tract must have been swallowed, not born.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; the case is where
The digestive tract (the way food passes out)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
For example, where he found it in the digestive tract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The found fish might be the non-kosher fish's own baby.
steps.terutzMaskana: Its location in the digestive tract proves it was swallowed.

steps.title: רב פפא: the fish was found in the gullet
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a similar answer: the fish was found in the gullet, where swallowed food passes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the case is where he found it in the passageway of the gullet.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers another answer of the same kind. He points to a different location that shows the fish was swallowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב ששת, he solves the problem by where the fish was found. He chooses the gullet, which clearly holds swallowed food and not babies.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For example, where he found it in the passageway of the gullet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 26, parallel to רב ששת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The found fish might have been born inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: A fish in the gullet was swallowed.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the fish was found whole and fully grown
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the fish was found whole and fully formed. It was not a tiny newborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: the case is where he found it whole.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a third answer, this time based on what the fish looks like rather than where it was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby fish born inside would be tiny and newly formed. A complete, grown fish shows that it was swallowed.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
For example, where he found it whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּצָאוֹ שָׁלֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 26, based on the fish's condition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case by the fish's condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The found fish might be a newborn.
steps.terutzMaskana: A whole, grown fish was swallowed, not born.

steps.title: רב אשי: most fish give birth to their own species
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that most fish give birth only to their own species. A kosher fish inside a non-kosher fish is therefore treated as if we saw it being swallowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: most fish give birth to their own kind, so it is as if it swallowed it in front of us.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes a completely different path. He rejects the whole worry from step 24 by using a רוב (majority).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher fish normally gives birth to non-kosher fish of its own kind. Based on this רוב, a kosher-species fish inside it is presumed not to be its baby, so we treat it as swallowed. According to רב אשי, it is permitted even if no one saw the swallowing, and the challenge of step 26 does not apply.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not just adding another case. He disagrees with the inference in step 24 that the fish is permitted only because we saw the swallowing.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four answers. רב ששת, רב פפא, and רב נחמן prove from the specific case that the fish was swallowed. רב אשי uses a general רוב: fish give birth only to their own species.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
most fish give birth to their own species,
and it is considered as if it swallowed in front of us.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רוֹב דָּגִים בְּמִינָן מַשְׁרִיצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 differently and undoes the inference of step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without seeing the swallowing, we would suspect the fish was born inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fish give birth to their own kind, so a kosher fish inside is assumed to have been swallowed.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: birth, eggs, nursing, and the bat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the whole ברייתא. Animals that give birth nurse their young, while animals that lay eggs gather food for them. The exception is the עטלף (bat), which lays eggs yet nurses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a non-kosher fish gives birth to live young, and a kosher fish lays eggs. Whatever gives birth nurses, and whatever lays eggs gathers food for its young, except the bat, which lays eggs and still nurses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the complete ברייתא it partly cited in step 25. This adds the extra rules about nursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real restatement of the source with more content, not a repeat of the argument. It sets up a general rule about how animals feed their young. The עטלף is singled out as an exception to that rule.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
a non-kosher fish gives birth to live young,
a kosher fish lays eggs,
whatever gives birth nurses,
and whatever lays eggs gathers food for its young,
except for the bat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּטִיל בֵּיצִים — מֵנִיק.
phrases.english: which, even though it lays eggs, nurses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the ברייתא partly cited in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals that give birth nurse their young, and animals that lay eggs gather food for them. The bat is the exception: it lays eggs yet nurses.
